chunks: From him, from Yunus, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) visited a man from his companions who was expiring, and he said: 'O Angel of Death, be kind to my companion, for he is a believer.'

He said: 'Receive glad tidings, O Muhammad, for I am kind with every believer. And know, O Muhammad, that when I capture the soul of a son of Adam, his family panics. So I stand in a corner of their house and say: 'What is this panic? By Allah, we did not hasten it before its appointed term, nor is there any sin for us in its capture.'

So if you are considerate and patient, you will be rewarded; and if you panic, you will sin and be burdened. And know that we have a return upon you, then another return. So beware, beware. There is no family in the east or west, of tents or of houses, except that I scan them five times a day.
And I am more knowing of their young and their old than they are of themselves. And if I wanted to capture the soul of a gnat, I would not have the power over it until my Lord commands me to do so.

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He only scans them during the times of prayer. So if he is among those who are regular in it at its times, he teaches him the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Angel of Death drives Iblis away from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the role of the Angel of Death in scanning families and how does prayer affect this process?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) reveals his daily inspection of human households, emphasizing that death is not premature but divinely timed. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) clarifies that this surveillance coincides with the five daily prayers, linking spiritual vigilance to the Angel's favor and the expulsion of Iblis from the dying believer. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the interplay between divine decree and the believer's ritual practice in securing a peaceful transition of the soul.
